Controlled feedback for the next round

Source: R/feedback.R
delphi_feedback.Rd

Prepares the controlled feedback that the experts receive before a further round: for each item to be rated again, the statistical response of the panel in the current round (median, quartiles and consensus) and, when available, the comments of the experts, reported anonymously. The feedback can be returned as a table or written to a document to be sent to the panel, in HTML or Word format.

Usage

delphi_feedback(
  x,
  file = NULL,
  round = NULL,
  items = NULL,
  comments = TRUE,
  title = "Delphi study: feedback for the next round",
  item_labels = NULL,
  threshold = 0.2,
  relative_to = c("points", "range"),
  method = c("wilcoxon", "scheibe", "both"),
  alpha = 0.05,
  scheibe = 0.15,
  type = 7,
  paired = NULL,
  open = interactive(),
  quiet = TRUE
)

Arguments

x

A delphi_data object.

file

Optional path of the feedback document, ending in .html or .docx. If NULL (default), no document is written.

round

Round on which the feedback is based. NULL (default) uses the last round; see delphi_status().

items

Items to include. By default, the items that require a further round on at least one indicator, according to delphi_status().

comments

Whether to include the comments of the experts on the selected items, when x contains comments (see delphi_add_comments()).

title

Title of the document.

item_labels

Optional named character vector with the full statement of each item. By default, the labels stored in x are used.

threshold, relative_to

Consensus rule, see delphi_consensus().

method, alpha, scheibe, paired

Stability rule, used to select the items for the next round; see delphi_stability().

type

Quantile algorithm; see delphi_describe().

open

Whether to open the document once it has been created.

quiet

Whether to suppress the rendering messages.

Value

A data frame of class delphi_feedback, invisibly when file is given, with one row per item and indicator and columns item, statement, indicator, round, n, median, q1, q3, iqr, consensus and status. The comments are stored in the attribute comments, a data frame with columns round, item and comment.

Details

The document is written for the experts: it explains the median and the interquartile range in plain words and contains no expert identifiers, no individual ratings and no information on the position of the authors of the comments. Comments are reproduced as written, so any detail that could identify their authors should be removed from the data beforehand. Writing a document requires the rmarkdown and knitr packages and Pandoc.

See also

delphi_status(), delphi_comments(), delphi_report().

Examples

x <- delphi_data(delphi_example, expert_col = "expert",
                 round_col = "round", indicator_col = "indicator",
                 scale = list(impact = c(1, 10), plausibility = c(1, 100)))
fb <- delphi_feedback(x, round = 1)
head(fb)
#>  item    indicator round  n median   q1    q3 consensus    status
#>    E2       impact     1 15      5  4.0  7.00     FALSE      open
#>    E2 plausibility     1 14     28 19.5 41.25     FALSE      open
#>    E4       impact     1 15      7  6.0  8.00      TRUE consensus
#>    E4 plausibility     1 15     63 58.0 82.00     FALSE      open
#>    E5       impact     1 15      4  3.0  8.50     FALSE      open
#>    E5 plausibility     1 15     30 14.0 87.00     FALSE      open
# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("rmarkdown", quietly = TRUE) &&
    rmarkdown::pandoc_available()) {
  out <- delphi_feedback(x, file.path(tempdir(), "feedback.html"),
                         round = 1, open = FALSE)
}
# }
